workflow.title: Keep a MacCleanse result selection separate from your saved cleanup preset
workflow.primaryIntent: Understand why unchecking one scan result is not the same as changing what future scans target.
workflow.description: MacCleanse's manual distinguishes one scan's selected results from its saved scan settings. Use that distinction to plan repeat maintenance without treating every large file as disposable; current v15 click paths remain untested.
outline: Lead with the saved-preset versus one-run selection distinction (C06), then official visual if permission clears.
Separate scan scope, result selection and erasure; explain the undated manual boundary, not an invented tested tutorial.
Review history/cookie categories for data the reader wants to keep; no blanket caches-safe claim.
Check future schedule and saved scope separately; never promise universal prompting (C05-C07).
Use the vendor's Large and Old caution (C11) as a backup/rebuild-cost review checkpoint.
Later comparison: Breathing Room, which we build, uses exact saved daily approvals but has preview, hosted and Python caveats (B01-B04).
workflow.interactionPass: Propose a non-mutating checklist with three columns: saved scan scope / this run's selected results / scheduled authority. No deletion commands, filesystem access or settings writes. Not implemented during research.
workflow.visualPlacement: Top: permission-cleared official Cleanup screenshot. Later: selected Breathing Room Space browser preview with full disclosure. Link-only is not a pass.
workflow.guardrails: No invented cache sizes, savings or usage anecdotes; no automation script that runs cleanup; no modern secure-erasure guarantee; no subscription total-cost winner.

comparison.title: Breathing Room vs MacCleanse: saved approvals or a cleanup suite?
comparison.primaryIntent: Choose by workflow: history/app cleanup with documented MacCleanse presets versus source-supported preview storage/process investigation and exact saved daily approvals.
comparison.lead: MacCleanse documents history cleanup, app removal and preset-based maintenance. Breathing Room, which we build, offers a different preview workflow around storage/process investigation and exact daily approvals. Neither is established here as safer, faster or a complete substitute for the other.
comparison.avoid: No duplicate alternatives page, winner checkmarks, unknown-as-No cells, fake testing or image-gate waiver.

maccleanseFits: Readers wanting the vendor-documented combination of histories/cookies cleanup, app uninstall/leftovers, duplicates and configurable recurring scans (C04-C05).
Readers wanting advertised version-only or lifetime-update purchase options rather than assuming a subscription is mandatory (C08).
maccleanseCautions: Pricing conditions/currency and actual checkout totals are unresolved; no cross-product cost winner.
Undated manual describes optional skip-to-erasing while also promising prompts; do not flatten conflicting modes (C07).
Documented erasure is not automatically recoverable Trash movement; no secure-deletion guarantee or safety benchmark (C11).
Legacy PowerPC trimming and old OS names are not proof of useful modern storage savings.
breathingRoomFits: Readers interested in source-supported storage ownership, grouped process/activity context and developer-cache discovery, accepting preview limitations (B01-B03).
Readers wanting a daily workflow based on exact saved approvals while the app remains running (B04).
breathingRoomCautions: Non-notarized preview, Python prerequisite and untested physical Intel behavior must remain prominent.
Hosted AI needs internet/authentication; relevant inspection context may leave the Mac; do not call it entirely offline.
Do not imply feature parity with MacCleanse's uninstaller, duplicate finder or history cleaning.
Optional automatic Ruff mode qualifies blanket approval statements; Trash moves do not prove reclaimed space.
